StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is exactly what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

InstanceType.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): StranglePower.instance_type = PowerInstanceType.INSTANCED_PER_APPLIER (sts2_rl/powers.py), mirroring StranglePower.cs:29. PowerCmd.apply's dispatch (sts2_rl/cmds.py) now finds an existing instance only when its applier matches this application's applier (mirroring FindExistingInstanceForStacking's InstancedPerApplier branch, PowerCmd.cs:170: `target.GetPowerInstances(id).FirstOrDefault(p => p.Applier == applier)`) -- a same-applier re-application still stacks via on_stack (unchanged), a different-applier one starts its own instance instead of merging. Verified by test/test_powers.py::TestPowerInstanceType::test_instanced_per_applier_same_applier_stacks_different_applier_splits. DORMANT stands: the only ported applier is the player (cards/mad_science.py), so a second applier is unreachable in current content. NOT closed by this fix: StranglePower's own before_card_played / on_card_played hooks have no applier filter at all (they fire for ANY card play, not just the applier's) -- a separate, pre-existing shape outside this guard's scope (instance dispatch, not the damage trigger's own filtering).  The text it replaced read: PowerInstanceType.InstancedPerApplier (StranglePower.cs:29) -- and per power_cmd gap G5's corrected census this is the ONLY ported InstancedPerApplier power in the game (the other is OblivionPower, unported). The sim keys stacking on the power id alone (cmds.py:308), so two appliers' Strangles on one target merge into a single instance with a single `_amounts` dict and a single amount, where C# keeps one instance per applier -- each of which deals its own damage per card play. Mechanism owned by power_cmd G5; not re-verdicted (rule 3). DORMANT in Ironclad scope: the only ported applier is the player, via Mad Science's Choking rider (cards/mad_science.py:134-136, `applier=ctx.player`), and there is exactly one player, so a second applier needs multiplayer or a monster-applied Strangle -- neither of which exists. This is the cleanest available statement of G5's InstancedPerApplier half: it is dormant *by scope*, not by content, so it will not become live by porting more Ironclad content. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

BeforeCardPlayed.rationale: StranglePower.cs:36-48 records `amountsForPlayedCards[cardPlay.Card] = base.Amount` for each card the applier's player plays; powers.py:2853-2856 keeps `self._amounts[id(card)] = self.amount`. The two C# guards -- `base.Applier?.Player == null` and `cardPlay.Card.Owner != base.Applier.Player` -- are single-player tautologies here because the only applier is the player. The DESIGN INTENT is preserved and is the subtle part: recording at BeforeCardPlayed is what stops Strangle triggering on the very card that applied it, since that card is already past its own BeforeCardPlayed -- the source's own comment (StranglePower.cs:18-21) says so and the sim's (powers.py:2849-2852) repeats it.

AfterCardPlayed.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: combat.py:574-600 now builds the play bracket INSIDE `for play_index in range(play_count)` -- `before_card_played` at :576 and `on_card_played` at :600 both fire once per replay iteration, mirroring CardModel.cs:1904-1965 (Hook.BeforeCardPlayed :1929 and Hook.AfterCardPlayed :1959, both inside the playCount loop). VERIFIED 2026-07-27 by reading `CombatState._resolve_card_play`. WAS: both fired once per logical play, outside the loop, so a Throwing-Axe- or Duplication-doubled card advanced every Before/AfterCardPlayed listener by 1 where the game advances it by 2.

AfterSideTurnEnd.rationale: Correct slot. The owner is an ENEMY -- Mad Science applies Strangle to its target (cards/mad_science.py:134-136) -- so C#'s `participants.Contains(base.Owner)` (StranglePower.cs:61) selects the enemy side, and Hook.AfterTurnEnd for the enemy side (Hook.cs:1267, CombatManager.cs:1256) is the sim's on_enemy_side_end (combat.py:345). Same correct-slot shape as tainted / high_voltage / territorial, and it means Strangle survives the whole enemy turn as C# intends. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: Strangle overrides no AfterRemoved, so the observable is identical -- the same mechanism note as power/no_draw's and power/tainted's.

guards.what: StranglePower.cs:52 `amountsForPlayedCards.Remove(card, out value)` keyed by CardModel
guards.rationale: The sim keys by `id(card)` (powers.py:2853, 2859). Equivalent for live cards -- the entry is written and popped inside one card play, so the object cannot be collected and its id cannot be recycled in between. Recorded because an id()-keyed dict is exactly the sort of shortcut that would be a gap if the entry outlived the play.

guards.what: powers.py:2860 `self.owner.is_gone` -> return, added by the sim
guards.rationale: C# has no such test; it relies on CreatureCmd.Damage refusing a dead target (damage_pipeline's step 1). The sim's check is earlier but the outcome is the same, and the dict entry is popped before the check on both sides, so no stale entry survives.

guards.what: The amount snapshot: damage = the amount AT BeforeCardPlayed, not at resolution
guards.rationale: C# stores base.Amount at BeforeCardPlayed and deals THAT value (StranglePower.cs:46, 55); powers.py:2856, 2859-2866 does the same. This is what makes a Strangle stacked mid-play deal the old amount, and it is preserved.
